R1785 replaces that step for the selected construction by an explicit pair proved free through Mathlib FreeGroup.injective_lift_of_ping_pong, with the existing exact rational 3-adic norm. No p-adic completion or projective quotient is introduced. All matrices, determinant identities, real embedding, near-identity bounds, signed-word denominators, growth bounds and entry separation are proved. Mathlib primary sources reused: GroupTheory/CoprodI, SubMulAction, Matrix/SpecialLinearGroup, Padics/PadicNorm, FreeGroup/Basic and rational casts. The signed-word convention matches FreeGroup.Lift.aux: true is positive and false is inverse. No strong Tits statement or source flattening theorem is assumed as an axiom. No novelty claim is made for this standard explicit ping-pong construction. It establishes the seed pair, not the full growing generator family in Lemma1.1 or any walk flattening theorem.

proof_scope: In progress. R1785 constructs q=3(n+1), a=(q+1)/q, A=diag(a,a^-1), M=[[1,1],[1,2]], B=M*A*M^-1. The map from the free group on two generators sending them to A,B is injective over both Q and R. A direct 3-adic ping-pong proof on nonzero rational vectors replaces the source strong-Tits invocation for this seed-pair step. Each entry error from identity is <=4/q and the squared ordinary Frobenius distance is <=(8/q)^2; inversion preserves that distance. Thus for every eta>0 some fixed n gives a free pair and their inverses inside the actual ball B_eta. With Q=q(q+1), every signed word of length ell has Q^ell as a common denominator and every entry has absolute value <=(1+8/q)^ell. Equal-length words representing different free-group elements differ in some real matrix entry by at least Q^(-ell). Word evaluation agrees exactly with Mathlib FreeGroup.lift/mk, including its sign convention. The larger near-identity family and actual-walk flatness are still unproved.

Keep the seed integer n fixed once sufficiently large; its q=3(n+1), Q=q(q+1) and growth factor s=1+8/q are universal constants as the target epsilon tends to zero. Concrete next theorem: a family of nonempty cyclically reduced equal-length words, pairwise distinct even up to inversion, has freely generating squares. Candidate proof uses the already-imported ping-pong lemma on FreeGroup Bool acting on itself by left multiplication. For each word w of length L, take the positive domain of reduced words with prefix w and the negative domain with prefix invRev(w). These domains are disjoint by equal length and distinctness. Prove that w^2 takes the complement of the negative domain into the positive domain: fewer than L letters cancel, leaving the first copy of w intact. Prove the inverse statement and nonempty domains. This candidate argument is NOT yet formalized. Handle the index-type nontriviality and L>0 explicitly. Mathlib FreeGroup/Reduce provides toWord, toWord_mul, toWord_inv, IsReduced.reduce_eq, reduction of a single letter, and reduced-word uniqueness; Basic supplies invRev and reduction relations. Do not mistake Nielsen–Schreier alone for a prescribed-basis/length theorem.

A simpler sufficient instance than all reduced source words may be positive words beginning with A and ending with B, with binary middle letters: for L>=2 there are2^(L-2) such words, and their squares have length2L. This still gives exponential cardinality; choose the fixed seed sufficiently close to identity so growth losses remain smaller than that exponential gain. After proving freeness and counting, implement a finite four-coordinate box pigeonhole argument for nearby matrices; using ambient dimension4 avoids requiring a sharp three-dimensional packing theorem. Prove that this translation preserves a free generating family (a Nielsen basis change), and derive the polynomial denominator/cardinality relations when L is proportional to log(1/epsilon). These are proposed next steps, not already-proved claims.
